rationale: The record is a political sociology/comparative state modernization article analysing isomorphism, decoupling, patronage, and legitimation in the state administrations of Thailand and Myanmar. Neither the title nor the bilingual abstract mentions water, sanitation, utilities, or household/community service access, failing Criterion 1 (E01: wrong topic) and Criterion 4.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Although the study discusses macro-level state administrations, bureaucracies, and neo-institutionalist governance concepts (relevant to plain Criterion 2 in the abstract), it is completely unrelated to water or sanitation service access and is excluded under both readings on Criterion 1 (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: Isomorphism and Decoupling: Processes of External and Internal Legitimation in Southeast Asia
How is it possible to analyse the seemingly contradictory modernization processes in Southeast Asian states?
Thailand and Myanmar are taken as case studies, because Thailand has always followed a strategy of international integration, in contrast to isolationist Myanmar.
